city: Hyderabad / Multi-state (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra)
parties: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Limited (KIMS) [Issuer]; Qualified Institutional Buyers including IFC, HSBC Mutual Fund, Edelweiss Mutual Fund, Axis Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, HDFC Life Insurance, Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance
headline: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences raises ₹1,500 crore via QIP at ₹755 per share
sum: KIMS successfully closed a ₹1,500 crore QIP on 19 June 2026, issuing 19,867,549 equity shares at ₹755 per share to institutional investors including IFC and leading Indian mutual funds and insurers. The proceeds are earmarked for debt repayment and subsidiary investments, strengthening the hospital chain's balance sheet as it expands capacity across multiple states.
implication: QIP pricing at ₹755 (below the ₹771.73 floor price, representing a 2.17% discount) reflects strong institutional appetite despite new-unit EBITDA erosion; the debt-reduction focus signals management prioritisation of balance-sheet stability over aggressive capex, a disciplined approach in a high-leverage expansion phase.
detail: The QIP opened on 16 June 2026 and closed on 19 June 2026, with allotment at ₹755 per share. The transaction increases paid-up equity capital from ₹8,002.78 lakh to ₹8,400.01 lakh, representing 4.73% dilution to pre-issue shareholders. Board approval was granted on 11 March 2026, followed by shareholder postal ballot clearance on 15 April 2026. Proceeds will be deployed primarily toward repayment of outstanding borrowings (estimated ₹1,000 cr per management guidance) and subsidiary capitalisation, supporting organic growth across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, and Maharashtra, where KIMS operates 26 hospitals with 7,300+ beds.

framework.ref: SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, Chapter VI
framework.note: Governs QIP eligibility, pricing, documentation, and allotment; floor price calculated under Regulation 176
Authorises equity issuance via special resolution; postal ballot procedure under Rule 17 of Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
framework.note: Mandates continuous disclosures, material event notifications (Regulation 30), trading window closures around fundraising decisions
Requires QIP completion within 365 days of special resolution; completion confirmed on 19 June 2026, well within deadline
Specifies floor price for QIP based on preceding 2 weeks' average weekly high/low closing prices
Defines QIBs and sets out restrictions on allottee lock-in (1 year on stock exchanges)
Governs tax treatment of premium received on share issuance

framework.ref: RBI Master Circular on External Commercial Borrowings
framework.note: Relevant to extent KIMS debt repayment includes ECB facilities (not explicitly disclosed in sources)

structure.consideration: ₹1,500 crore (gross proceeds); 19,867,549 equity shares of ₹2 face value each issued at ₹755 per share
conditions: Shareholder special resolution approval via postal ballot on 15 April 2026
Finance & Investment Committee approval of final issue price on 19 June 2026
100% primary issuance (no offer for sale by promoters)
Allottees restricted from selling on recognised stock exchanges for 1 year from allotment
approvals: Shareholders via postal ballot (15 April 2026, e-voting period 17 March–15 April 2026)
Finance & Investment Committee (19 June 2026 for final pricing)
BSE and NSE in-principle approval (implicit via preliminary placement document filing)
structure.novel: Emphasis on institutional investor participation (IFC, leading MFs and insurers) signalling strong market confidence; debt reduction focus rather than capex-primary use, differentiating from typical healthcare QIPs; pricing 2.17% below floor price demonstrates strong book-building despite Q4 FY26 PAT decline of 58.25% YoY due to new-unit startup costs.

triggers.note: QIP route is election by issuer; triggers mandatory private placement to QIBs only, floor pricing, and allottee lock-in
Equity issuance requires special resolution passed by shareholders; triggers postal ballot procedure
Material event disclosures at each gate: board approval (11 Mar), shareholder approval (15 Apr), opening (16 Jun), closure & allotment (19 Jun)
Eligibility gate: KIMS must be listed for 18 months (listed 28 Jun 2021, so requirement satisfied)
